cond_0001.intro: Performs a wide variety of electronic or electro-mechanical assembly operations on assemblies or sub-assemblies. Determines and/or follows methods and sequence of operations in performing wiring, component installation, hand soldering and cable harnessing on assembly units.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Build cable, harnessing and mechanical assemblies.
Position and align parts and components. Secure them in place or remove them using appropriate, various methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Install assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Perform initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Tend to machines that prepare or assemble parts.
Build printed wiring board assemblies and perform rework and modifications of prototype boards.
Assist engineers in building bread boards.
Assist engineers with sheet metal modifications.
Build setups and adjustments holding tolerances to blueprint specifications.
Read and interpret work orders and follow drawings or sample assemblies to facilitate assembly work.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
2 Or more years of experience performing electro-mechanical assembly with an emphasis on cable/harness rework and electronic/electrical soldering and termination.
Skilled knowledge of cable and harness rework and fabrication including pinning and depinning, various termination methods, labeling and dressing, wire routing, splicing, etc.
Excellent SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) skills.
Proficient ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret for work performance.
Ability to follow procedures and adhere to regulations related to work being performed.
Ability to lift, push and pull up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.
Preferred Requirements
Skilled ability using hand tools, limited power tools, soldering irons including under a microscope, and basic machining equipment.
Applies acquired job skills and company policies and procedures to complete assigned tasks.
Receives assignments, scheduling and assembly instructions from Lab Supervisor and Lead person.
Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognizes the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice.
Normally follows established procedures on routine work and requires instructions only on new assignments.

People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of electrical assembly and wiring work.
cond_0022.responsibilities:
Build cable, harnessing and mechanical assemblies.
Position and align parts and components. Secure them in place or remove them using appropriate, various methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Install assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Perform initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Tend to machines that prepare or assemble parts.
Build printed wiring board assemblies and perform rework and modifications of prototype boards.
Assist engineers in building bread boards.
Assist engineers with sheet metal modifications.
Build setups and adjustments holding tolerances to blueprint specifications.
Read and interpret work orders and follow drawings or sample assemblies to facilitate assembly work.
cond_0022.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
2 Or more years of experience performing electro-mechanical assembly with an emphasis on cable/harness rework and electronic/electrical soldering and termination.
Skilled knowledge of cable and harness rework and fabrication including pinning and depinning, various termination methods, labeling and dressing, wire routing, splicing, etc.
Excellent SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) skills.
Proficient ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret for work performance.
Ability to follow procedures and adhere to regulations related to work being performed.
Ability to lift, push and pull up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.
Preferred Requirements
Skilled ability using hand tools, limited power tools, soldering irons including under a microscope, and basic machining equipment.
Applies acquired job skills and company policies and procedures to complete assigned tasks.
Receives assignments, scheduling and assembly instructions from Lab Supervisor and Lead person.
Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognizes the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice.
Normally follows established procedures on routine work and requires instructions only on new assignments.
cond_0022.values: We value responsibility, respect, and a genuine commitment to doing right by others. We aim to create outcomes that are fair, thoughtful, and beneficial to the people we serve.

cond_0224.intro:
We are looking for an Electrical Assembler to join our team, working on in-flight entertainment systems on planes for some of the most recognized airlines across the globe. In this role, you will take ownership of assembly, rework, and improvement of [Product name masked] IFE systems, executing hands-on electrical and electro-mechanical work to a high standard.
If you've ever boarded a plane with a video display on the seat in front of you, offering Movies, TV, Gaming, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Audio, there's a great chance that [Company name masked] is behind it all. We are looking for skilled assemblers to join our Technical Services Team and help us continue to deliver best-in-class services.
cond_0224.responsibilities:
You will own a wide variety of electronic or electro-mechanical assembly operations on assemblies or sub-assemblies. You will determine and/or follow methods and sequence of operations, executing wiring, component installation, hand soldering, and cable harnessing on assembly units.
Build cable, harnessing, and mechanical assemblies.
Position and align parts and components. Secure or remove them using appropriate methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Install assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Execute initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Operate machines that prepare or assemble parts.
Build printed wiring board assemblies and lead rework and modifications of prototype boards.
Support engineers in building bread boards.
Support engineers with sheet metal modifications.
Build setups and adjustments holding tolerances to blueprint specifications.
Read and interpret work orders and follow drawings or sample assemblies to direct assembly work.
cond_0224.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent.
2 Or more years of experience performing electro-mechanical assembly with an emphasis on cable/harness rework and electronic/electrical soldering and termination.
Skilled knowledge of cable and harness rework and fabrication including pinning and depinning, various termination methods, labeling and dressing, wire routing, splicing, etc.
Excellent SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) skills.
Proficient ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret for work performance.
Ability to lift, push, and pull up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting, and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.
Preferred Requirements
Skilled ability using hand tools, limited power tools, soldering irons including under a microscope, and basic machining equipment.
Ability to follow procedures and adhere to regulations related to work being performed.
Applies acquired job skills and company policies and procedures to complete assigned tasks.
Receives assignments, scheduling, and assembly instructions from Lab Supervisor and Lead person.
Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognizes the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice.
Normally follows established procedures on routine work and requires instructions only on new assignments.

cond_0297.responsibilities:
Work with the team to build cable, harnessing, and mechanical assemblies.
Coordinate with colleagues to position and align parts and components. Secure or remove them using appropriate methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Support the installation of assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Help bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Assist in performing initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Tend to machines that prepare or assemble parts.

Work alongside engineers to help build bread boards.

Proficient ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret for work performance.
Ability to follow procedures and adhere to regulations related to work being performed.
Ability to lift, push, and pull up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting, and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.

Excellent SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) skills.

cond_0309.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
cond_0309.responsibilities:
Build cable, harnessing and mechanical assemblies.
Position and align parts and components. Secure them in place or remove them using appropriate, various methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Install assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Perform initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Tend to machines that prepare or assemble parts.
Build printed wiring board assemblies and perform rework and modifications of prototype boards.
Assist engineers in building bread boards.
Assist engineers with sheet metal modifications.
Build setups and adjustments holding tolerances to blueprint specifications.
Read and interpret work orders and follow drawings or sample assemblies to facilitate assembly work.
cond_0309.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent, or equivalent practical experience.
Around 2 years of experience performing electro-mechanical assembly, with a focus on cable/harness rework and electronic/electrical soldering and termination.
Working knowledge of cable and harness rework and fabrication, including pinning and depinning, various termination methods, labeling and dressing, wire routing, splicing, etc.
Familiarity with SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) techniques.
Ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret them for work performance.
Comfort using hand tools, soldering irons (including under a microscope), and basic machining equipment.
Ability to lift, push, and pull up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting, and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.
Preferred Requirements
Experience following procedures and adhering to regulations related to work being performed.
Ability to apply acquired job skills and company policies to complete assigned tasks with some independence.
Comfortable working on semi-routine assignments and recognizing when to deviate from standard practice.
Able to follow established procedures on routine work and take direction on new assignments.

cond_0481.intro: We are looking for an Electrical Assembler to join our team, working on, replacing, and improving the performance of in-flight entertainment systems on planes for some of the most recognized airlines across the globe. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of electro-mechanical assembly and wiring work.
cond_0481.responsibilities:
Build cable, harnessing and mechanical assemblies.
Position and align parts and components. Secure them in place or remove them using appropriate, various methods including soldering, crimping, fastening, gluing, etc.
Install assemblies in cases or cabinets.
Bundle and route wiring within the product being worked.
Perform initial tests to check for faulty parts, continuity, etc.
Tend to machines that prepare or assemble parts.
Build printed wiring board assemblies and perform rework and modifications of prototype boards.
Assist engineers in building bread boards.
Assist engineers with sheet metal modifications.
Build setups and adjustments holding tolerances to blueprint specifications.
Read and interpret work orders and follow drawings or sample assemblies to facilitate assembly work.
cond_0481.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent.
Must have 2 or more years' experience performing electro-mechanical assembly with an emphasis on cable/harness rework and electronic/electrical soldering and termination.
Must have skilled knowledge of cable and harness rework and fabrication including pinning and depinning, various termination methods, labeling and dressing, wire routing, splicing, etc.
Must have excellent SMT (surface mount technology) and THT (through-hole technology) skills.
Must have proficient ability to read schematic diagrams and blueprints and interpret for work performance.
Skilled ability to using hand tools, limited power tools, soldering irons including under a microscope, and basic machining equipment.
Ability to follow procedures and adhere to regulations related to work being performed.
Applies acquired job skills and company policies and procedures to complete assigned tasks.
Receives assignments, scheduling and assembly instructions from Lab Supervisor and Lead person.
Works on assignments that are semi-routine in nature but recognizes the need for occasional deviation from accepted practice.
Normally follows established procedures on routine work and requires instructions only on new assignments.
Ability to lift, push and pull from up to 40 lbs. On a daily basis.
Ability to perform repetitive motion including bending, twisting and various hand and arm movements.
Ability to stand and sit for extended periods.
